comment_box: I write in opposition to the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) proposal to restrict abortion access and care for veterans and their loved ones.    Access to abortion care and counseling is essential to a person’s freedom to make decisions about their health and well-being and to have control over their economic security. It is a matter that should only concern the pregnant person and their doctor.  This proposed rule is an insult to all who have served and their loved ones. VA has a mandate to provide needed care to veterans, and this includes abortion care and counseling without barriers. For veterans, who face unique health needs or who may be survivors of military sexual assault, access to abortion is necessary to live safe and healthy lives. VA should be expanding abortion access given the current public health crisis - not taking it away.    Contrary to VA’s reasoning, this proposed rule would harm those who rely on the Department for care. It does nothing to protect the health and lives of our veteran communities. Under this proposed rule, pregnant veterans will once again fear punishment, be forced to travel hundreds or thousands of miles, or delay their care until they are on the brink of death in order to access the abortion care they need. This new policy will force many veterans to remain pregnant against their will, including survivors of sexual assault and veterans experiencing mental health issues.     All veterans and their loved ones deserve access to abortion - without restrictions or political interference. I strongly oppose the this proposed rule.
